# What SonarQube tokens the library redacts, and what it leaves alone.
#
# Every token here is built from the ordered run 0123456789abcdef, which no real
# credential is: a body is forty hexadecimal characters, so the run twice over
# and eight more of it are one, and the four character prefix in front brings a
# token to forty-four.

patterns: sonarqube-token

# The four prefixes SonarQube writes a token with, in the places a token is
# written: the environment a build reads it from, the property an analysis is
# handed it in, the request that authenticates with it, and the URL a badge is
# rendered from.

case:     a user token in an environment assignment
in:       SONAR_TOKEN=squ_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      SONAR_TOKEN=«sonarqube-token»

case:     a project analysis token in the property an analysis reads
in:       sonar-scanner -Dsonar.token=sqp_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      sonar-scanner -Dsonar.token=«sonarqube-token»

case:     a global analysis token in a json body
in:       {"token":"sqa_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567"}
out:      {"token":"«sonarqube-token»"}

case:     a project badge token in the url a badge is rendered from
in:       https://sonarqube.example.com/api/project_badges/measure?project=my-project&metric=alert_status&token=sqb_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      https://sonarqube.example.com/api/project_badges/measure?project=my-project&metric=alert_status&token=«sonarqube-token»

# The alphabet the forty characters behind a prefix are written in: lowercase
# hexadecimal, which is what the generator's hexadecimal encoder writes. A
# letter outside it or a character of either case above it ends the body, and
# the prefix is read in the one case SonarQube writes it.

case:     a letter outside hexadecimal in the body
in:       squ_0123456789abcdefg123456789abcdef01234567
out:      squ_0123456789abcdefg123456789abcdef01234567

case:     an uppercase body
in:       squ_0123456789ABCDEF0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      squ_0123456789ABCDEF0123456789abcdef01234567

case:     an uppercase prefix
in:       SQU_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      SQU_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567

case:     a hyphen where the prefix carries its underscore
in:       squ-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      squ-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567

case:     a character naming no kind SonarQube writes
in:       sqx_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      sqx_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567

# The lengths either side of forty. The count is what twenty random bytes come
# to in hexadecimal, and it is read as a count rather than a floor:
# thirty-nine characters are not a token, and forty-one are a token and one
# character that belongs to no credential. The second of those is the price of
# having no boundary behind the match — a boundary there would drop this token
# rather than trim it, and a real token written against a hexadecimal character
# would come through whole.

case:     a body of forty characters is a token
in:       squ_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      «sonarqube-token»

case:     a body of thirty-nine characters is not
in:       squ_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456
out:      squ_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456

case:     a hexadecimal run longer than a token is a token and what follows it
in:       squ_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef012345678
out:      «sonarqube-token»8

# What a token may be written against. The prefix is the whole of the anchor and
# there is no boundary on either side of it, so a token keeps its span whatever
# word character it abuts.

case:     a token after an underscore
in:       SONAR_TOKEN_squ_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      SONAR_TOKEN_«sonarqube-token»

case:     a token after a letter
in:       xsqu_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      x«sonarqube-token»

case:     a token before a hyphenated word
in:       squ_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567-suffix
out:      «sonarqube-token»-suffix

case:     a token at the end of a sentence
in:       the token is squ_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567.
out:      the token is «sonarqube-token».

# Two tokens written together, and a prefix written where a body would stand.
# A body carries no character a prefix opens with, so the second of these is one
# token standing where a candidate failed rather than two tokens overlapping.

case:     two tokens with nothing between them
in:       squ_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567sqa_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      «sonarqube-token»«sonarqube-token»

case:     a prefix written where a body would stand
in:       squ_squ_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      squ_«sonarqube-token»

# What this pattern redacts that nobody issued. Every character of a prefix
# belongs to base64url, so a payload written in that alphabet can spell one, and
# where forty hexadecimal characters follow it those forty-four are redacted.
# That is the answer rather than a fault in it, because sparing it would spare a
# real token: the vendor's format is that prefix and those forty characters, and
# no part of it is left for such a run to fail. Standard base64 and hexadecimal
# write no underscore at all, so neither carries a candidate at however long it
# runs.

case:     a prefix inside a longer base64url run
in:       payload=zzzzsqu_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567zzzz
out:      payload=zzzz«sonarqube-token»zzzz

case:     a standard base64 payload, which carries no underscore
in:       payload=MIIBIjANBgkqhkiG9w0BAQEFAAOCAQ8AMIIBCgKCAQEAsqu0123456789abcdef
out:      payload=MIIBIjANBgkqhkiG9w0BAQEFAAOCAQ8AMIIBCgKCAQEAsqu0123456789abcdef

# And what this pattern leaves alone. First the prefix SonarQube Cloud
# identifies a scoped organization token by, written to the width the one
# ruleset reading that format asks for and to the width the other kinds are
# written to: the pattern's own file says what is missing, which is a width
# SonarQube states. Then the shape a token took before these prefixes, forty
# hexadecimal characters carrying nothing to be recognised by but the property
# name beside them — the same run a commit hash is written as, which is why such
# a token reaching a log stays in the output whole. Then a body a space has
# broken, a run of the right length opening with no prefix, and a line of prose.

case:     a scoped organization token at the width the ruleset asks for
in:       sqco_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789a
out:      sqco_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789a

case:     a scoped organization token at the width the other kinds are written to
in:       sqco_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      sqco_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567

case:     the shape a token took before a prefix was written in front of one
in:       sonar.login=0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      sonar.login=0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567

case:     a body broken by a space
in:       squ_0123456789abcdef 123456789abcdef01234567
out:      squ_0123456789abcdef 123456789abcdef01234567

case:     a run of the right length opening with no prefix
in:       xxx_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      xxx_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567

case:     prose
in:       there is no credential in this sentence
out:      there is no credential in this sentence

case:     a log line naming the server a token authenticates against
in:       time=2026-08-17T00:00:00Z level=info msg="analysis finished" url=https://sonarqube.example.com/dashboard?id=my-project
out:      time=2026-08-17T00:00:00Z level=info msg="analysis finished" url=https://sonarqube.example.com/dashboard?id=my-project
